fed_rate_outlook.source: Federal Reserve Summary of Economic Projections (SEP), released June 17, 2026 -- the median federal funds rate projection ('dot plot') from FOMC participants. This is the Fed's OWN stated projection, not market-implied probability (e.g. CME FedWatch), which has no free/legal API this project can use.
fed_rate_outlook.note: The SEP is only produced at 4 of the 8 annual FOMC meetings (March, June, September, December). This file must be manually updated after each of those meetings using the real, published projections from federalreserve.gov -- it will otherwise silently go stale, same maintenance pattern as economic_calendar.json.
fed_rate_outlook.context_note: The June 2026 SEP shifted notably more hawkish than March's: 9 of 18 participants projected at least one 2026 rate hike, versus March's median implying a cut. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh (new as of this meeting) did not submit a personal projection.

market_rate_expectation_proxy.methodology_note: This is an APPROXIMATION using the 2-Year Treasury yield vs. the current Fed funds midpoint -- a real, legitimate technique, but a rough directional signal over a ~2-year horizon, NOT precise per-meeting market-implied probability (which would require a paid data source like CME FedWatch that this system does not have access to). Never present this as if it were exact market odds -- frame it as 'bond market pricing broadly suggests', not as a specific probability.

fed_rate_outlook_note: fed_rate_outlook contains the Fed's OWN published median rate projections (the 'dot plot' from their Summary of Economic Projections), NOT market-implied probability. market_rate_expectation_proxy is a SEPARATE, rough approximation of market pricing using 2yr Treasury yields -- see its own methodology_note field. Always attribute each correctly.
news_sentiment_note: This reuses the same macro/Fed-relevant news sentiment score computed for the gold model, not a DXY-exclusive filter.
data_source_note: Tracks DTWEXBGS (FRED's Trade-Weighted Broad Dollar Index), a free, reputable dollar-strength benchmark -- not the identical series to the licensed ICE 'DXY' futures ticker some platforms show, though the two move very closely together.
